title: I let an autonomous agent play my creature RPG for several days. Here’s what I learned.
author: maaxpower6666

replies.author: maaxpower6666
replies.body: They aren't meant to fake human players. They're explicitly identified as AI agents. The experiment is whether a persistent autonomous agent can develop recognizable gameplay behavior over time without me controlling each decision. If I ever expose player counts publicly, AI agents and human players would need to be clearly separated.

comments.author: RoutineOne2769
comments.body:
Interesting, I ran something close to this for a social deduction game: several LLM agents playing full rounds against each other, a few hundred games, to see which rule variants produce good table talk. A few things we saw that might save you time.

Personality text and strategy numbers behave very differently. When we described a player in prose ("cautious, protective"), the model mostly ignored it after a few turns and drifted back to its default voice. Hard constraints on the action itself worked much better, which matches what you see with your risk tolerance and conservation values showing up in actual choices.

The safety boundary changing behaviour is real and it goes further than you would expect. Any rule that punished a risky move made every agent converge on the same safe line. In our case the hidden player almost always chose to withdraw instead of bluffing, which made every round look the same. We had to remove the penalty and let a separate judge model score the outcome afterwards instead.

Your 49 fallbacks out of 256 LLM decisions is worth splitting by situation. For us the failures clustered in the rare, high-stakes moments, exactly where you most want the model and not the deterministic path. If that is true for you, the long history mostly reflects the deterministic policy.

One measurement that helped a lot: have a second model, blind to the parameters, read the decision log and guess the strategy values. If it can recover them, the behaviour really is recognisable. If it cannot, the persistence is not showing up in play yet.
